def-m-out-of-n-bootstrap-and-subsampling:
## Definition

Let $n\ge1$ be an integer, let $(\mathcal Z,\mathcal C)$ be a measurable observation space, let $P$ be a probability law on it, and let $Z_1,\ldots,Z_n$ be IID $P$-distributed sampling units ([[def-identically-distributed-and-iid-random-variables]]). For each $1\le k\le n$, let $T_k$ be a measurable real-valued statistic and write $\widehat\theta_k=T_k(Z_1,\ldots,Z_k)$; the target is a scalar $\theta(P)$ and $a_k>0$ is its declared normalization at sample size $k$. The empirical law
$$P_n:=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\delta_{Z_i}$$
is a probability law by [[lem-finite-empirical-measure-is-a-probability-law]].

For an integer $1\le m\le n$, the **m-out-of-n bootstrap** draws $Z_1^*,\ldots,Z_m^*$ conditionally IID from $P_n$ and computes
$$R_{m,n}^{*}:=a_m\bigl(T_m(Z_1^*,\ldots,Z_m^*)-\widehat\theta_n\bigr).$$
The conditional distribution of this root given the observed sample is the bootstrap approximation. The ordinary n-out-of-n bootstrap is the case $m=n$ and uses $a_n$.

For $1\le m<n$, **subsampling without replacement** chooses a subset $I=\{i_1<\cdots<i_m\}$ uniformly from the $\binom{n}{m}$ subsets of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$ and computes
$$R_{m,n}^{\mathrm{sub}}:=a_m\bigl(T_m(Z_{i_1},\ldots,Z_{i_m})-\widehat\theta_n\bigr).$$
Its conditional law is the uniform distribution over those subsets. With replacement and without replacement are distinct conditional laws, even though both use the same declared statistic $T_m$.

The asymptotic regime considered on this page has integer $m=m_n\to\infty$ and $m_n/n\to0$. The resampled root uses the actual size-$m$ scale $a_m$; validity does not follow merely from this regime. For inference based on a centered root, the scale ratio $a_m/a_n\to0$ is an additional root-specific centering condition when it is used. A design with dependent sampling units requires a separate design-matched resampling procedure. This definition does not identify a bootstrap law with a Bayesian posterior or a design-randomization law. Extrapolation from several resample sizes is not asserted here; it requires a separate proof of the source-specific regular expansion and remainder regime.
lem-uniform-cdf-order-and-quantile-cover:
## Statement

For a cumulative distribution function $F$ and $u\in(0,1)$, define the generalized quantile $q_F(u):=\inf\{x\in\mathbb R:F(x)\ge u\}$, and put $q_F(0):=-\infty$ and $q_F(1):=+\infty$. Let $X$ be a real random variable with CDF $F$. In part 3, a **random CDF** $\widehat G$ means that each $\widehat G(x)$ is measurable and, almost surely, $x\mapsto\widehat G(x)$ is a right-continuous CDF. For $\varepsilon,\delta\ge0$ and $0\le\alpha_1,\alpha_2<1$ with $\alpha_1+\alpha_2<1$, the following hold.

1. If $G$ is a CDF and $\sup_x(G(x)-F(x))\le\varepsilon$, then $\mathbb P\{X\le q_G(1-\alpha_2)\}\ge1-\alpha_2-\varepsilon$.
2. If $G$ is a CDF and $\sup_x(F(x)-G(x))\le\varepsilon$, then $\mathbb P\{X\ge q_G(\alpha_1)\}\ge1-\alpha_1-\varepsilon$.
3. If $\widehat G$ is a random CDF and $\mathbb P\{\sup_x|\widehat G(x)-F(x)|\le\varepsilon/2\}\ge1-\delta$, then
$$\mathbb P\{q_{\widehat G}(\alpha_1)\le X\le q_{\widehat G}(1-\alpha_2)\}\ge1-\alpha_1-\alpha_2-\varepsilon-\delta.$$

The endpoints $\alpha_i=0$ use the extended quantiles and make the corresponding tail event vacuous. No continuity of $F$ or absence of atoms at the target quantiles is required.
lem-pointwise-cdf-convergence-to-a-conti:
## Statement

Let $F$ be a continuous CDF and $(G_n)$ random CDFs, meaning that each $G_n(x)$ is a measurable real random variable and, almost surely, $x\mapsto G_n(x)$ is a right-continuous CDF. Suppose that for each fixed $x\in\mathbb R$, $G_n(x)\to F(x)$ in probability. Then
$$\sup_{x\in\mathbb R}|G_n(x)-F(x)|\longrightarrow0$$
in probability.
lem-bernoulli-root-laws-are-uniformly-we:
## Statement

For $n\ge1$ and $p\in[0,1]$, let $\mu_{n,p}$ be the law of
$$S_{n,p}:=\frac1{\sqrt n}\sum_{i=1}^n(B_i(p)-p),$$
where $B_1(p),\ldots,B_n(p)$ are IID Bernoulli$(p)$. For every $p,q\in[0,1]$,
$$\pi(\mu_{n,p},\mu_{n,q})\le |p-q|^{1/3},$$
where $\pi$ is the Levy–Prokhorov metric. The bound is uniform in the sample size and choice-free.
thm-ordinary-bootstrap-fails-for-uniform:
## Statement

For each integer $n\ge1$, let $X_1,\ldots,X_n$ be IID with the uniform law on $[0,1]$, let $M_n=\max_{i\le n}X_i$, and set the support endpoint $\theta=1$. The sampling root is $R_n=n(M_n-1)$. For the ordinary n-out-of-n bootstrap, draw $n$ observations IID from the empirical law $P_n$ and set $R_n^*=n(M_n^*-M_n)$. Here weak conditional consistency means that for every bounded continuous real function $f$, the conditional expectation $\mathbb E^*[f(R_n^*)]$ converges in probability to $\mathbb E[f(R_n)]$. With $h(x)=(1-2|x|)_+$, a bounded continuous function, the conditional bootstrap expectation $\mathbb E^*[h(R_n^*)]$ stays asymptotically separated from $\mathbb E[h(R_n)]$. Therefore the ordinary bootstrap is not weakly conditionally consistent at this support endpoint.
thm-m-out-of-n-resampling-valid-for-unif:
## Statement

For each $n\ge1$, let $X_1,\ldots,X_n$ be IID uniform on $[0,1]$, $M_n=\max_{i\le n}X_i$, and $R_n=n(M_n-1)$. Let $m=m_n$ be integers with $1\le m_n<n$ for all sufficiently large $n$, $m_n\to\infty$, and $m_n/n\to0$. Form the conditional m-out-of-n bootstrap and subsampling roots
$$R_{m,n}^{*}=m(M_{m,n}^{*}-M_n),\qquad R_{m,n}^{\mathrm{sub}}=m(M_{I}-M_n),$$
where $M_{m,n}^{*}$ is the maximum of $m$ draws with replacement from $P_n$, and $M_I$ is the maximum over a uniformly selected m-subset. For each method, its conditional CDF converges uniformly in probability to
$$F(x)=\begin{cases}e^x,&x<0,\\1,&x\ge0.\end{cases}$$
This is also the limiting CDF of the actual m-root $m(M_m-1)$. Here first-order validity means that the conditional CDF converges in probability to this actual-root limit; the theorem asserts no uniform validity over other distribution classes.
thm-uniform-subsampling-coverage-under-r:
## Statement

Let $\mathcal P$ be a nonempty class of IID laws on a measurable observation space. For $P\in\mathcal P$, let $\theta(P)\in\mathbb R$ be a target, let $\widehat\theta_k$ be a measurable estimator at every sample size $k$, and let $a_k>0$ be deterministic. Put
$$R_{n,P}=a_n(\widehat\theta_n-\theta(P)),\qquad J_{n,P}(x)=P^{\otimes n}(R_{n,P}\le x),$$
and define $H_{m,P}$ as the CDF of the actual size-$m$ root $a_m(\widehat\theta_m-\theta(P))$. Let $m=m_n$ be integers with $1\le m_n<n$ for all sufficiently large $n$, $m_n\to\infty$, and $m_n/n\to0$; for centered resampling roots, assume $a_m/a_n\to0$. Let $\widehat H_{m,n}$ be the conditional CDF of either $a_m(\widehat\theta^*_{m,n}-\widehat\theta_n)$ for the m-out-of-n bootstrap or $a_m(\widehat\theta_{I,m}-\widehat\theta_n)$ for uniform subsampling without replacement, as defined in [[def-m-out-of-n-bootstrap-and-subsampling]], with each evaluation measurable and almost surely right-continuous sample paths.

Suppose the following exact root-law and feasible-root conditions hold:
$$\limsup_{n\to\infty}\sup_{P\in\mathcal P}\sup_x\{H_{m,P}(x)-J_{n,P}(x)\}\le0,\qquad \limsup_{n\to\infty}\sup_{P\in\mathcal P}\sup_x\{J_{n,P}(x)-H_{m,P}(x)\}\le0,$$
and for every $\eta>0$,
$$\sup_{P\in\mathcal P}P^{\otimes n}\!\left(\sup_x|\widehat H_{m,n}(x)-H_{m,P}(x)|>\eta\right)\longrightarrow0.$$
For $0\le\alpha_1,\alpha_2$ with $\alpha_1+\alpha_2<1$, define
$$I_n=\left[\widehat\theta_n-\frac{q_{\widehat H_{m,n}}(1-\alpha_2)}{a_n},\ \widehat\theta_n-\frac{q_{\widehat H_{m,n}}(\alpha_1)}{a_n}\right].$$
Assume the interval endpoints are measurable functions of the data and set $\mathcal C_n=\{Q\in\mathcal P:\theta(Q)\in I_n\}$. Then
$$\liminf_{n\to\infty}\inf_{P\in\mathcal P}P^{\otimes n}\{P\in\mathcal C_n\}\ge1-\alpha_1-\alpha_2.$$
If only the first one-sided CDF comparison holds, the upper root quantile gives the corresponding one-sided lower confidence bound; if only the second holds, the lower root quantile gives the one-sided upper confidence bound. The m-regime alone does not imply any of these CDF conditions. Weak convergence of root laws alone is not a substitute for the stated uniform comparisons and feasible-root control.
thm-bootstrap-fails-at-nonsmooth-boundar:
## Statement

Assume AC. For each integer $n\ge1$, let $X_1,\ldots,X_n$ be IID $N(0,1)$ and let $\bar X_n=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^nX_i$. At $\mu=0$, which is the boundary value of the nonnegative ranges of $g_1(\mu)=|\mu|$ and $g_2(\mu)=\mu^2$, consider these two functionals. For the ordinary bootstrap, draw $X_1^*,\ldots,X_n^*$ conditionally IID from the empirical law and write $W_n^*=\sqrt n(\bar X_n^* -\bar X_n)$ with conditional CDF $G_n^*$. The conditional empirical-bootstrap CLT [[thm-conditional-iid-bootstrap-clt-for-empirical-law]], specialized to $d=1$, $a=1$, and $\sigma^2=1$, gives $G_n^*(x)\to\Phi(x)$ in probability for every fixed $x$, where $\Phi$ is the standard normal CDF. Here conditional weak consistency means that the conditional integral of every bounded continuous test function converges in probability to its sampling-law integral.

Then the ordinary bootstrap is inconsistent for both correctly centered roots
$$R_{n,1}=\sqrt n\,|\bar X_n|,\qquad R_{n,1}^*=\sqrt n\,(|\bar X_n^*|-|\bar X_n|),$$
and
$$R_{n,2}=n\bar X_n^2,\qquad R_{n,2}^*=n\bigl((\bar X_n^*)^2-\bar X_n^2\bigr).$$
In both cases the true root CDF is continuous at zero with value zero, whereas the conditional bootstrap root CDF at zero stays away from zero with positive probability. The first functional is nonsmooth at the boundary; the second has zero first derivative there, so its nondegenerate sampling root is on the second-order scale.
